newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH AGENCY WANTS TO UP MIN GRAIN PRICES IN '97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH AGENCY WANTS TO UP MIN GRAIN PRICES IN '97.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), the food market regulator, said it had recommended to the government that the minimum price of wheat should rise to 520 zlotys a tonne in 1997 from 400 zlotys this year.

The ARR said in a statement it also proposed that the minimum price of rye rise to 380 zlotys a tonne from 280 zlotys and that the minimum price of milk increase to 0.58 zlotys a litre next year from 0.50 zlotys in 1996.
Minimum prices, which have to be approved by the government to become law, serve as the base for establishing the ARR's intervention prices, which can be up to 20 percent higher than the minimum.
The statement said the government should debate the minimum price proposals at an upcomminng cabinet meeting on the ARR's annual market intervention programme.
It also said that the 1997 budget draft, presetnly debated in parliament, allocated some 85.6 million zlotys for ARR food market intervenions next year, up from 80.9 million this year.
